en.template: Help me build a Nairobi-to-remote-bookkeeping transition plan using {salary}, {savings}, {status}, {restrictions}, {clients}, {software} and {quotes}. Separate training, compliance and paid-pilot gates. Model collections after fees and restricted tax/health reserves, stress-test client loss and FX, and keep me employed unless every exit condition is met no earlier than November 2027. Ask before contacting anyone, opening accounts, sharing client data or submitting forms.

phases.title: Research official certification costs, payment routes, Kenyan tax rules and data-protection basics
phases.note: Certifications and job-board rates, payment routes into Kenya, tax and data-protection rules
phases.judgment: It took back a claim it could not support: a KES 750 bank fee had been noted as visually confirmed, and the colleague removed that and marked the bank tariff as unverified.

phases.title: Build the guide and a transparent shilling-and-dollar transition model
phases.note: Resignation conditions up front, a fee table with arithmetic, and a month-by-month runway
phases.judgment: The recommendation is cautious by design: certification is the easy part (the official QuickBooks and Xero routes are free), but the job examples also ask for experience and several exclude Kenyan applicants, so the guide says to stay employed and consider resigning from November 2027 at the earliest, after three qualifying collection months.

phases.title: Independently verify the figures and sources, and test the page on desktop and phone
phases.judgment: The independent check recomputed 270 figures with zero discrepancies, yet still flagged a timing mismatch: January counts USD 150 of incoming payments while first client outreach is scheduled for February. It also listed what it could not verify, such as bank fees and Kenya-specific earnings.

workers: Checked Kenyan tax and registration rules, plus data-protection and contract basics for handling US and UK client data
Checked what QuickBooks Online and Xero certifications cost and require, whether Kenyans can enrol, and dated offshore bookkeeping job rates
Compared ways of being paid into Kenya (Payoneer, Wise, bank transfer) with their fees and eligibility rules
Recomputed every figure on its own and checked the claims against the source list
